story.title: Story 2: Finalization Boundary Between Live State and Archive

result.reviewScopeSummary: Reviewed Story 2 against its story/spec/test-plan, then verified the finalization seam across `ArchiveFinalizationService`, the user-response and execution hooks, process-history compatibility, and the Story 2 server/client tests. I also ran the configured story and epic gates plus an ad hoc runtime reproduction of execution-result archiving.

newFindings.title: Execution-result archive rows are keyed to transient provider IDs instead of the persisted live history items
newFindings.evidence: `ProcessEnvironmentService.applyExecutionResultSideEffects` persists each execution history item first, but then calls `appendFromProcessHistoryItem` with the original provider payload instead of the stored row (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/process-environment.service.ts:690-706`). `ArchiveFinalizationService.appendFromProcessHistoryItem` derives `sourceObjectId` and `finalizationKey` directly from `historyItem.historyItemId` (`apps/platform/server/services/archive/archive-finalization.service.ts:57-93`). Both the in-memory store and the real Convex mutation generate fresh history IDs/createdAt values when appending history (`apps/platform/server/services/projects/platform-store.ts:3144-3153`, `convex/processHistoryItems.ts:93-119`). An ad hoc reproduction returned `storedHistoryIds` `["pr:history-process_message-1"]` while the archive entry used `sourceObjectId` `"runtime-model-1"` and `finalizationKey` `"model:runtime-model-1"`. That means the canonical archive is not actually bridged from the persisted current-history row, and later history-based reconciliation would target a different identity. The current TC-2.3b test encodes the transient provider ID instead of checking the stored history row (`tests/service/server/archive-finalization.test.ts:252-257`).

productionPathFindings: The real execution-result hook archives the pre-persistence provider object instead of the persisted `processHistoryItems` row, so production archive identity diverges from the live-history identity even though duplicate suppression still passes.
additionalObservations: `green-verify` and `verify-all` both passed, but the current Story 2 tests miss the identity mismatch because TC-2.3b asserts the provider-supplied `runtime-model-1` ID rather than the stored history row returned by `appendProcessHistoryItem`.

Live/archive separation itself is otherwise evidenced well: `tests/service/server/process-live-updates.test.ts:306-372` and `tests/service/client/process-live.test.ts:243-274` both show websocket/reducer history upserts do not create archive rows.
I did not find a fake adapter or placeholder branch wired into the runtime finalization path; the blocking issue is a real production data-link mismatch in the execution completion hook.
